1771.title: The flood of 1771, an estimate, on the town of about 1788
1771.caption: The "Great Fresh" of May 1771: about 38.0 ft above sea level (NAVD88) at the City Locks, give or take 3 ft, from diaries via an Army Corps figure. Dark: water at the level; pale band: ground under water at the top of the range.
notes: Off the river's channel, {floodAcres} acres under water. Of the {buildings} buildings this view shows, {floodBuildingsInWater} stand in water, {floodDepthAtBuildingsMedianFt} ft deep at the median, {floodDepthAtBuildingsMaxFt} ft at the deepest.

The city as it stood in 1788 as far as the record shows: buildings standing today by their year built, plus those traced from fire-insurance maps; what was lost and not traced is missing. The ground is today's lidar.
A bathtub fill: water at the level wherever it connects to the river, not a model of the flood.
Drawn with isoscape (ROUGH DRAFT d1). Levels: USGS and NOAA records, checked; see the series notes.
